final_candidates.decision_summary: Located in antigenic site Sa, K157T achieves top-tier antibody escape while demonstrating outstanding sequence plausibility to maintain replication fitness.
D172N confers robust immune escape with maximal PLM compatibility, ensuring high viral viability and structural tolerance.
Situated in antigenic site Sb/Ca, K185E provides potent antigenic escape coupled with high structural compatibility and strong evolutionary prevalence.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates have strong convergent evidence balancing high antibody escape and preservation of replication fitness.

history.rationale: Position 156 lies in the prominent Sa antigenic loop where charge introduction drives antibody escape. It is well tolerated in influenza H1 DMS replication assays.
While escape prediction is high, both PLM and ProteinMPNN indicate severe structural and fitness penalties.
G156E severely impairs structural compatibility (0.064) and has 0% homolog frequency and low PLM score, risking loss of replication fitness.

rejection.reason: G156E severely impairs structural compatibility (0.064) and has 0% homolog frequency and low PLM score, risking loss of replication fitness.

history.rationale: Located at the apex of antigenic site Sa, K157 is a frequent target of neutralizing antibodies. Substitution to Asn removes positive charge, conferring strong escape while maintaining replication fitness.
K157N shows strong escape potential and solid PLM support, introducing a functional glycosylation site motif at the antigenic apex.
K157N is a strong antigenic escape variant, though K157T is slightly preferred based on sequence plausibility.
An alternative substitution at antigenic site Sa that disrupts antibody binding epitopes. Threonine is chemically well tolerated on the solvent-exposed surface.
K157T exhibits the highest antibody escape score and exceptional PLM fitness support, making it an ideal balanced candidate.
K157T combines exceptional escape potential (EVEscape 0.929) with outstanding sequence plausibility (ESM-1v 0.930). It remains our top candidate.
Position 158 is a canonical antigenic drift hotspot in site Sa. The S158N substitution alters antibody contacts while preserving local loop conformation.
S158N shows high structural compatibility and solid escape potential, retaining viability well.
S158N introduces potential glycosylation/steric shielding with excellent structural compatibility (0.928) and notable MSA frequency (13.6%).
Position 170 is surface-exposed in the 160-loop region flanking antigenic sites. Asn substitution neutralizes the basic residue to evade binding while preserving structural integrity.
Solid escape and reasonable structural accommodation, despite weak PLM score.
K170N has solid escape and structural tolerance, with moderate natural occurrence (13.6%), though low ESM-1v.
Part of the Ca antigenic site on the HA head. Loss of the negative charge mediates escape from site-directed antibodies with minimal perturbation to head domain folding.
D172N combines near-maximal sequence PLM plausibility with very strong predicted antibody escape.
D172N exhibits high immune escape and maximal ESM-1v plausibility (1.000), making it an extremely robust escape mutation.

Position 185 is a core residue of antigenic site Sb near the receptor-binding pocket. Charge reversal to Glu strongly perturbs neutralizing antibody binding while retaining functional receptor binding.
Strong escape and high structural compatibility support K185E, though sequence PLM plausibility is low.
K185E demonstrates substantial natural evolutionary prevalence (32.7% of homologs in Swiss-Prot MSA) and strong structural compatibility (0.892), mitigating ESM-1v hesitation.
Neutral polar substitution at antigenic site Sb that avoids unfavorable electrostatic interactions with antibodies. Known to support robust viral replication.
Perfect structural compatibility delta, but moderate escape and very low PLM support.
While structurally favored, K185T is absent in Swiss-Prot homologs and ranks below K185E.
Adjacent to the receptor binding site within epitope Sb, K187 mutations disrupt key monoclonal antibody footprints. Asn is compatible with local loop packing and fitness.
Moderate escape and structural tolerance, penalized by low PLM plausibility.
K187N shows moderate structural compatibility but zero homolog frequency and low ESM-1v.
Position 143 belongs to antigenic site Ca2 and frequently mutates in seasonal H1 drift. Tyr introduces steric alterations conferring escape while sustaining HA stability.
Lower escape score compared to top candidates and poor PLM plausibility.
H143Y offers moderate escape but weak sequence plausibility and no structural coordinate coverage.
